key_test: two-sided paired t-test of per-participant mean identification RT, correct rejections (meanRT_cr) vs misses (meanRT_miss); effect size dz = t/sqrt(n)
exclusions: none at participant level; the shipped aggregate Agg_priming_ANOVA.dat averages all classified test trials (no misidentification filter, although the protocol text excludes misidentified study/test trials)
agreement: all three agree on the aggregate file: table t(31)=2.40 p=.023 d=.424; R t=2.3977 p=0.02271 d=0.42; Python t=2.3977 p=0.022709 dz=0.4239
notes: Anchored on the script's test, which matches the report's key effect. Trial-level check from Analysedaten_1.sav (5440 rows; phase 2, SDT_category 1-4): aggregating ALL labelled test trials reproduces every participant's meanRT_cr and meanRT_miss exactly (32/32), so the aggregate applies no identification filter. Applying the protocol's stated rule changes the numbers: excluding test misidentifications gives t(31)=2.136, p=.0407, t/sqrt(n)=.378; excluding study and test misidentifications drops participant 20 (no miss trials left) and gives t(30)=2.427, p=.0215. Same direction and significance either way. R ran with the remote helper source() line dropped and getOSFfile pointed at the local copy of OSF btr65; httr/RCurl skipped (only the helper used them). compute.es::des returns d = 0.42 (it passes the t/sqrt(n) value through).
